5437-an-original-belle.title: An Original Belle

5437-an-original-belle.description: A book by Col. Charles H. Weygant, to the recollections of Capt. Thomas. She was rather commonplace at first, but circumstances led her to the endeavor to be true to her own nature and conscience and to adopt a very simple scheme of life. She achieved no marvellous success, nothing beyond the ability of multitudes like herself.

arxiv-2208-04349.title: Coordinated Per-Antenna Power Minimization for Multicell Massive MIMO Systems with Low-Resolution Data Converters Thanks: Y. Cho and B. L. Evans are with the 6G@UT Research Center, Wireless Networking and Communication Group (WNCG), Dept. of Electrical and Computer Engineering, The University of Tex
arxiv-2208-04349.creator: Yunseong Cho, Graduate Student Member, IEEE, Jinseok Choi, Member, IEEE,
arxiv-2208-04349.description: Abstract † † footnotetext: This work was presented in part at the IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference (IEEE WCNC) , Austin, Texas, April 2022 [ 1 ] . A multicell-coordinated beamforming solution for massive multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) systems is presented when employing low-resolution data converters and per-antenna level constraints.

arxiv-2305-08631.title: Information Reconciliation for High-Dimensional Quantum Key Distribution using Nonbinary LDPC codes Thanks: We acknowledge funding from: The Center of Excellence SPOC (ref DNRF123)
arxiv-2305-08631.creator: Ronny Müller 2 , Davide Bacco 1 , Leif Katsou Oxenløwe 2 , and Søren Forchhammer 2
arxiv-2305-08631.description: Abstract Information Reconciliation is an essential part of Quantum Key distribution protocols that closely resembles Slepian-Wolf coding. The application of nonbinary LDPC codes in the Information Reconciliation stage of a high-dimensional discrete-variable Quantum Key Distribution setup is proposed. We model the quantum channel using a q q -ary symmetric channel over which qudits are sent.

arxiv-2305-14623.title: Self-Checker: Plug-and-Play Modules for Fact-Checking with Large Language Models
arxiv-2305-14623.creator: Miaoran Li, Baolin Peng, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao, Zhu Zhang
arxiv-2305-14623.description: Abstract Fact-checking is an essential task in NLP that is commonly utilized to validate the factual accuracy of a piece of text. Previous approaches mainly involve the resource-intensive process of fine-tuning pre-trained language models on specific datasets. In addition, there is a notable gap in datasets that focus on fact-checking texts generated by large language models (LLMs).

arxiv-2306-10398.title: Periodic solutions in next generation neural field models
arxiv-2306-10398.creator: Carlo R. Laing, Oleh E. Omel’chenko
arxiv-2306-10398.description: Abstract We consider a next generation neural field model which describes the dynamics of a network of theta neurons on a ring. For some parameters the network supports stable time-periodic solutions. Using the fact that the dynamics at each spatial location are described by a complex-valued Riccati equation we derive a self-consistency equation that such periodic solutions must satisfy.

arxiv-2410-13050.title: Improved control of Dirichlet location and scale near the boundary
arxiv-2410-13050.creator: Catherine Xue, Alessandro Zito, Jeffrey W. Miller
arxiv-2410-13050.description: Abstract Dirichlet distributions are commonly used for modeling vectors in a probability simplex. When used as a prior or a proposal distribution, it is natural to set the mean of a Dirichlet to be equal to the location where one wants the distribution to be centered.

arxiv-2411-05438.title: Inhomogenous Navier–Stokes equations with unbounded density
arxiv-2411-05438.creator: Jean-Paul Adogbo, Piotr B. Mucha, Maja Szlenk
arxiv-2411-05438.description: Abstract In the current state of the art regarding the Navier–Stokes equations, the existence of unique solutions for incompressible flows in two spatial dimensions is already well-established. Recently, these results have been extended to models with variable density, maintaining positive outcomes for merely bounded densities, even in cases with large vacuum regions.

arxiv-2502-19382.title: Functional central limit theorems for non-local branching Markov processes
arxiv-2502-19382.creator: Christopher B. C. Dean, Emma Horton *
arxiv-2502-19382.description: Abstract The aim of this paper is to study the fluctuations of a general class of supercritical branching Markov processes with non-local branching mechanisms. We establish functional central limit theorems and show that the limiting behaviour falls into three regimes, determined by the size of the spectral gap associated with the first-moment semigroup of the branching process.

arxiv-2602-12285.title: From Biased Chatbots to Biased Agents: Examining Role Assignment Effects on LLM Agent Robustness
arxiv-2602-12285.creator: Linbo Cao, Lihao Sun, Yang Yue
arxiv-2602-12285.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents capable of actions with real-world impacts beyond text generation. While persona-induced biases in text generation are well documented, their effects on agent task performance remain largely unexplored, even though such effects pose more direct operational risks.

pmc-10526955.title: A TLR4 Agonist Induces Osteosarcoma Regression by Inducing an Antitumor Immune Response and Reprogramming M2 Macrophages to M1 Macrophages
pmc-10526955.creator: Iseulys Richert, Paul Berchard, Lhorra Abbes, Alexey Novikov, Kamel Chettab, Alexandra Vandermoeten, Charles Dumontet, Marie Karanian, Jerome Kerzerho, Martine Caroff, Jean-Yves Blay, Aurélie Dutour
pmc-10526955.description: Simple SummaryDue to the lack of progress in OsA’s treatment and survival, there is a need to develop new therapeutic approaches for this tumor. OsA is a complex tumor for which the immune microenvironment appears as a potential therapeutic option. This study explores the antitumor effect of a chemically detoxified TLR4 agonist MP-LPS, under liposomal formulation called Lipo-MP-LPS.

pmc-10624927.title: A low dietary sodium dose is associated with a more pronounced aldosterone response in normotensive than in hypertensive individuals
pmc-10624927.creator: Niels Graudal, Thorbjørn Hubeck-Graudal, Gesche Jurgens
pmc-10624927.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). In this comprehensive meta-regression analysis encompassing 79 randomized controlled trials, we observed that in populations assigned to a high sodium intake level exceeding 94 mmol, there was no discernible link between plasma aldosterone levels and sodium intake.

pmc-11325531.title: Small cell lung cancer associated small bowel obstruction, a diagnostic conundrum: A case report
pmc-11325531.creator: Mohammad Ayoub, Mohannad Natheef AbuHaweeleh, Nabil Mahmood, Colin Clelland, Malak Mohammad Ayoub, Harman Saman
pmc-11325531.description: Key clinical messageSmall cell lung cancer (SCLC), a neuroendocrine aggressive subtype of lung cancer, is associated with paraneoplastic disorders in about 9% of patients. In this report, we describe a middle‐aged man who presented with chronic bowel obstruction caused by chronic intestinal pseudo‐obstruction (CIPO) due to SCLC.

pmc-11367106.title: Effectiveness of a guided digital self-help intervention to improve sleep and the biological clock in university students – Study protocol for a randomized controlled trial
pmc-11367106.creator: Laura M Pape, Annemieke van Straten, Sascha Y Struijs, Philip Spinhoven, Niki Antypa
pmc-11367106.description: BackgroundSleep problems occur in many university students which affects their mental health and daily functioning. Cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) has been proven effective in adults but research in university students, who struggle to maintain a 24-hour rhythm, is still limited.

pmc-11421174.title: Initial signs in patients with ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms: time for an expanded triad?
pmc-11421174.creator: Peter Bergmark, Mitra Sadeghi, Mareia Talvitie, Rebecka Hultgren
pmc-11421174.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background and objectiveMisdiagnosis of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms (rAAA) contributes to delayed treatment and potentially higher mortality. The symptomatology in patients with rAAA is complex and challenging, 25–50% presumably fulfill the criteria of the standard triad of signs (STS).

pmc-12602316.title: Low-intensity transcranial focused ultrasound neuromodulation of the amygdala: is left always right?
pmc-12602316.creator: Annakarina Mundorf, Sebastian Ocklenburg
pmc-12602316.description: to the growing field of non-invasive brain stimulation, and the authors are to be commended for the technical precision and clinical ambition of their approach. While employing a technically advanced methodology, the study’s fixed approach of stimulating only the left amygdala may limit treatment responsiveness in some patients due to interindividual differences in brain lateralization.

pmc-13194579.title: Capability, opportunity, and motivation: a structural equation model of hand hygiene behavior based on the COM-B framework in a Chinese hospital setting
pmc-13194579.creator: Wenjing Jiang, Xia Li, Li Cao, Yuhan Zhang, Ping Zhou, Chunli Song, Xiaoli Chen, Yiju Xie, Juan Tang
pmc-13194579.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundHealthcare-associated infections (HAIs) present a major threat to patient safety worldwide. While hand hygiene is the primary defense against HAIs, compliance among healthcare workers (HCWs) remains inadequate, highlighting a persistent “know-do” gap.

pmc-13224339.title: Pan-immune inflammation value and neutrophil-to-albumin ratio predict hemorrhagic transformation after intravenous thrombolysis in acute ischemic stroke: a dual-center cohort study
pmc-13224339.creator: Zhuang Zhu, Yao Geng, Hualin Wang, Bo Du, Min Xu, Kefan Yi, Jiaxin Shi, Xufeng Wang, Yongsheng Yuan, Deqin Geng, Kezhong Zhang
pmc-13224339.description: Background and purposeHemorrhagic transformation (HT) remains a critical complication of intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) in acute ischemic stroke (AIS), yet reliable pre-thrombolysis predictors are limited. We investigated whether pan-immune inflammation value (PIV) and neutrophil-to-albumin ratio (NAR), individually and in combination, are associated with HT and its subtypes.MethodsIn this dual-center retrospective cohort study, 4,313 AIS patients treated with IVT were included.
